blocks.text: Chat fine-tuning applies supervised fine-tuning specifically to multi-turn conversational data, teaching a model to hold a coherent dialogue, maintain a consistent persona, and handle system level instructions across an entire conversation rather than just answering isolated single turn requests well.
This topic focuses on what makes chat fine-tuning specifically different from general SFT, building directly on the Conversation Dataset and Chat Templates topics covered earlier in this course.
1. What Chat Fine-Tuning Specifically Targets

blocks.alt: Single turn SFT is compared against chat fine-tuning, which targets multi-turn behavior

blocks.text: While general SFT can train a model on any labeled task, chat fine-tuning is specifically aimed at the behaviors that only show up across multiple turns, remembering earlier context, maintaining a consistent voice, and gracefully handling topic shifts, none of which a purely single turn dataset can teach directly.
2. Multi-Turn Coherence as the Core Goal

blocks.alt: Turn three correctly remembers information established in turn one

blocks.text: The central goal of chat fine-tuning is coherence, a later turn in a conversation should correctly reflect and build on information established earlier, rather than contradicting it or behaving as if the conversation had just started fresh.

This depends directly on the quality of the conversation dataset covered in the earlier Conversation Dataset topic, since a model can only learn to be coherent from examples that themselves demonstrate coherent multi-turn behavior.
3. Persona and Tone Consistency

blocks.alt: Examples with a consistent persona produce a stable persona at inference time

blocks.text: Chat fine-tuning also shapes how consistently a model maintains its intended persona and tone across a conversation, friendly, formal, concise, whichever voice the training examples consistently demonstrate tends to become the model default across turns, not just within a single response.

blocks.title: Consistency needs to be trained into every turn, not just the first
blocks.content: A dataset with a strong persona in the opening turn but drifting inconsistency in later turns teaches the model that drift is acceptable, undermining the whole point of persona training.

blocks.text: 4. Handling System Prompts During Chat Fine-Tuning

blocks.alt: A system prompt gets applied consistently across every turn

blocks.text: Since a system prompt is meant to shape behavior across an entire conversation, chat fine-tuning examples need to demonstrate the model actually respecting that system level instruction consistently through every turn, not just in its first response.
5. Refusals and Safety Behavior in Chat Models

blocks.alt: An unsafe request is paired with a correct refusal example

blocks.text: Chat fine-tuning datasets often include examples of appropriately declining unsafe, harmful, or out of scope requests, teaching the model a consistent, correctly worded refusal pattern rather than leaving that behavior entirely to a later alignment training stage.

This overlaps with, but is distinct from, the deeper alignment work covered in this course dedicated Alignment Training module, chat fine-tuning establishes baseline refusal behavior through labeled examples, while alignment training further tunes that behavior using human preference signals.
6. Chat Fine-Tuning Data Sources

blocks.alt: Real chat logs are compared against simulated dialogues as data sources

blocks.text: Chat fine-tuning data draws from the same two broad sources covered in the earlier Conversation Dataset topic, real collected conversations and synthetically simulated ones, with the same tradeoffs, realism versus control and speed of collection, applying directly here.

blocks.text: 7. Evaluating a Chat Fine-Tuned Model

blocks.alt: Multi-turn evaluation includes a context retention check

blocks.text: Evaluating chat fine-tuning quality requires testing the model across genuine multi-turn interactions, specifically checking whether it correctly retains and uses information from earlier turns, rather than only evaluating isolated single turn responses in an otherwise multi-turn deployed product.
8. Common Failure Modes in Chat Fine-Tuning

A chat fine-tuned model that was trained on too little multi-turn data, or data with poor context consistency, often shows telltale symptoms, forgetting details from earlier turns, drifting persona over the course of a long conversation, or failing to correctly apply a system prompt after the first response.
9. Chat Fine-Tuning as Part of a Larger Pipeline

Chat fine-tuning typically sits alongside, not instead of, task specific SFT covered in an upcoming topic, a deployed conversational assistant often needs both, the ability to hold a coherent dialogue and the ability to correctly perform whatever specific tasks it is asked to help with along the way.
Worked Example

A team fine-tuning a customer support chat assistant builds a dataset of genuine multi-turn support conversations, each one checked for context consistency, does the assistant correctly remember the customer order number mentioned in turn two when responding in turn five.

After training, they specifically test the deployed model with long, multi-turn conversations rather than only single turn spot checks, catching and fixing one case where the model lost track of an account tier mentioned early in a conversation, a problem their earlier single turn evaluation had completely missed.
Common Mistakes

items: Training exclusively on single turn data and expecting genuine multi-turn coherence to emerge on its own
Allowing persona or tone to drift across turns within the training data itself
Only evaluating a chat fine-tuned model with isolated single turn tests rather than genuine multi-turn conversations
Assuming refusal behavior trained into SFT data alone is sufficient without any further alignment work for a safety sensitive deployment

blocks.text: Practice

Take a five turn conversation you have written or collected, and check specifically whether the final turn genuinely depends on information from an earlier turn, if it does not, extend the example so it does, since that is exactly what chat fine-tuning data needs to demonstrate.
Key Takeaway

Chat fine-tuning applies supervised fine-tuning specifically to multi-turn conversational data, and its value comes from teaching context retention, persona consistency, and system prompt adherence across turns, behaviors that cannot be learned from single turn data alone and need to be both trained and evaluated at the conversation level.
